title: Hardwood Mulch vs. Dyed Mulch: Which Lasts Longer in Chicago Weather?
intro: Chicago homeowners understand the relentless demands our unique climate places on outdoor spaces. A well-maintained garden bed or foundation planting isn't just about aesthetics; it's about resilience. Mulch acts as a protective barrier, regulating soil temperature by keeping roots cooler in summer and warmer in winter. It conserves precious moisture, reducing the need for frequent watering – a significant benefit during dry spells. Furthermore, mulch effectively suppresses weeds, saving you countless hours of laborious pulling, and as organic materials decompose, they slowly enrich the soil, improving its structure and fertility over time. For Chicago homeowners, understanding these fundamental benefits is the first step toward making an informed mulch choice.
